newsitem.title: CHINA: China's evaded income taxes total $144 million.
newsitem.headline: China's evaded income taxes total $144 million.

text.p: Chinese taxpayers have evaded personal income taxes worth an estimated 12 billion yuan ($144.6 million) since the tax was introduced in 1980, and authorities plan to toughen tax laws, the China Economic News said on Thursday.
Many Chinese, not used to paying taxes during the rule of communist ideologue Mao Zedong, failed to report extra income such as money earned from second jobs, the newsletter said.
Tax authorities will revise the tax law to impose punishment for tax evasion, it said.
"Many people are not yet used to drawing money from their pockets for tax payment," the newsletter said.
A poor tax collection system has also contributed to the losses in tax income, it said.
"Tax collection work is hampered by inadequate staff, lack of operational funds, high costs and backward conditions for collection and administration," it said.

Although personal income taxes collected from January to April in 1996 were up 20 percent compared with the same period last year to 5.2 billion yuan, the amount of evaded taxes was growing even faster, it said.
"The actual amount collected is far behind the nominal growth of such taxes from year to year and the present status of the collection can hardly be said (to be) optimistic," it said.
